the identification of the source of metal ions, which caused the precipitation and the characterization of metal-induced conjugate protein aggregation.
the identification and characterization of the metal-leachate-induced precipitation of a protein-based conjugated antigen.
the identification and characterization of the metal-leachate-induced instability of a conjugate vaccine.

the precipitation was due to metal-induced aggregation and denaturation of the antigen.

the metal leachate from the hosebarb fittings caused precipitation of the antigen conjugate by forming complexes with the antigen peptide.
trace metal ions in the conjugate vaccine solution can lead to significant loss of protein tertiary structure.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of metal-containing materials should be avoided during development and manufacture of protein-based vaccines.
the presence of trace amounts of metal ions can cause precipitation of conjugates, and this may be a common problem for conjugates that contain histidine residues in their antigen peptide.
metal ions in trace amounts can have a significant impact on conjugate stability and should be considered when designing conjugate vaccines.
